The '''2010–11 [[Super League Greece]]''' was the 75th season of the highest [[Association football|football]] league of Greece and the fifth under the name ''Super League''. The league consisted of 16 teams, the 13 best teams of the [[2009–10 Super League Greece|2009–10 season]] and three teams that had been promoted from the [[2009–10 Beta Ethniki]].

The season began on 27 August 2010 with the first matches of the regular season<ref>{{cite web|title=Schedule of the 2010–11 season|url=http://www.superleaguegreece.net/schedule|publisher=[[Super League Greece]]|access-date=6 January 2011| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101224025314/http://superleaguegreece.net/schedule| archive-date= 24 December 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> and ended on 25 May 2011 with the last matches of the [[#European playoffs|European playoff round]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Super League Greece – Champions Öeague qualifiers Play-off fixtures and results|url=https://int.soccerway.com/national/greece/super-league/2010-2011/champions-league-qualifiers-play-off/matches/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211115719/https://int.soccerway.com/national/greece/super-league/2010-2011/champions-league-qualifiers-play-off/r14289/matches/|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 December 2019|website=Soccerway}}</ref> [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] were the defending champions, having won their 20th Greek championship in the [[2009–10 Super League Greece|2009–10 season]].
The season was marred by [[Koriopolis]], a match-fixing scandal which involved several teams from the top three leagues of Greek football.

==Season overview==

===Title race===
The league was won by [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]], who earned their 38th Greek league title. They finished with a 13-point lead over runners-up [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]], who had to compete in a [[#Playoffs|play-off round]] which determined the exact allocation of spots for both European competitions.

Panathinaikos was joined in the play-offs by third-placed club and city rivals [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]], fourth-placed [[PAOK FC|PAOK]] and fifth-placed [[Olympiacos Volos F.C.|Olympiacos Volos]]. Panathinaikos eventually won the play-off group and thus earned the second Greek spot in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]]. Since AEK had already won the [[2010–11 Greek Cup]] competition a few weeks earlier and thus were already qualified for the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League]], both PAOK and Olympiacos Volos were guaranteed a spot in that competition as well.

===Relegation===
{{See also|Koriopolis}}
After thirty matches, the relegation spots were occupied by 14th-placed [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]], 15th-placed [[Athlitiki Enosi Larissa F.C.|AEL]] and last-placed [[Panserraikos F.C.|Panserraikos]]. However, all three clubs eventually stayed in the league after [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis Thessaloniki]], [[Kavala F.C.|Kavala]] and [[Olympiacos Volos F.C.|Olympiacos Volos]] were demoted by separate sports court decisions.

On 19 May 2011, [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis Thessaloniki]] were denied a licence for the 2011–12 season over unpaid debts and thus demoted to the second-level [[Football League (Greece)|Football League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Αnnouncement for the teams receiving UEFA licence for the 2011–12 season (in greek) |url=http://www.epo.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=18771:2011-04-20-12-07-48&catid=83:2010-02-22-21-13-22&Itemid=291 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110426115413/http://www.epo.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=18771:2011-04-20-12-07-48&catid=83:2010-02-22-21-13-22&Itemid=291 |archive-date=26 April 2011 |access-date=16 May 2011 |work=Hellenic Football Federation |publisher=epo.gr}}</ref> Soon afterwards, the Thessaloniki club was found guilty of having [[forgery|forged]] documents during the winter transfer window and put at the end of the standings.<ref name=IraklisPlacedLast/>

A few days after the Iraklis verdict, it became evident that several clubs and officials throughout the top leagues of Greek football were involved in a [[Koriopolis|match-fixing scandal]]. Investigations in the matter were taken all summer. On 28 July 2011, Kavala and Olympiacos Volos were found guilty of having taken part in illegal actions and were therefore demoted to the Football League.<ref name=VolouKavala>{{cite web|title=Υποβιβάζονται Ολυμπιακός Βόλου και Καβάλα!|url=http://www.enet.gr/?i=news.el.a8lhtismos&id=297022|publisher=Enet.gr|access-date=28 July 2011}}</ref> However, both clubs appealed to the decision and they stayed in the [[Super League Greece]], though they were deducted 8 and 10 points respectively.<ref name=VolouKavala /> On 11 August 2011, [[UEFA]] disqualified Olympiacos Volos from further participation in the UEFA Europa League.<ref name="Olympiakos Volou excluded from Europa League">{{cite web|title=Differdange to replace Olympiacos Volou|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01f4-0e79263028b4-8b2d1ac70c5c-1000--differdange-to-replace-olympiacos-volou/|publisher=UEFA|access-date=15 August 2011|date=11 August 2011}}</ref> On 23 August 2011, the Professional Sports Committee stripped Kavala and Olympiacos Volos of their professional licence due to their chairmen's involvement in the scandal.<ref name="Olympiakos Volou and Kavala relegated to Delta Ethniki"/>

==Teams==
[[Levadiakos F.C.|Levadiakos]], [[PAS Giannina F.C.|PAS Giannina]] and [[Panthrakikos F.C.|Panthrakikos]] had been relegated at the end of the [[2009–10 Super League Greece|2009–10 season]] after finishing in the bottom three places of the league table. Levadiakos concluded a four-year run in the highest football league of Greece. Panthrakikos finished a two-year tenure with the league, while PAS Giannina had to return to the [[Football League Greece|Football League]], formerly known as ''Beta Ethniki'', after just one season.

The three relegated teams were replaced by [[2009–10 Beta Ethniki]] champions [[Olympiacos Volos F.C.|Olympiacos Volos]], runners-up [[A.O. Kerkyra|Kerkyra]] and promotion playoff winners [[Panserraikos F.C.|Panserraikos]]. Olympiacos Volos returned to the Greek top football level after 20 seasons. Kerkyra ended a three-year absence from the Super League, while Panserraikos immediately returned to the league.

==Play-offs==
In the play-off for Champions League, the four teams play each other in a home and away [[Round-robin tournament|round robin]]. However, they do not all start with 0 points. Instead, a weighting system applies to the teams' standing at the start of the play-off mini-league. The team finishing fifth in the Super League started the play-off with 0 points. The fifth placed team's end of season tally of points is subtracted from the sum of the points that other teams have. This number is then divided by five and rounded to the nearest whole number of points, if necessary, to give the other teams the points with which they start the mini-league.

Fifth-placed club Olympiacos Volos earned 47 points during the regular season. Based on this number and the calculations above, Panathinaikos as runners-up began the play-offs with three points ((60–47)/5 = 2.6, rounded up to 3), while AEK Athens started with one point ((50–47)/5 = 0.6, rounded up to 1) and PAOK with no points ((48–47)/5 = 0.2, rounded down to 0).
